industry.src: AR FY2025-26 (SIAM and Vahan tables), Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls, GAM Research
themes: Motorcycles up to 350cc went from 28% to 18% GST: domestic motorcycles +6.6% in FY26 (13.06 mn), with a weak first half and a boom after September. Price rises from April 2026 handed back 30-40% of the cut (management).
Hurts KTM 390, Dominar 400 and Triumph 400s; Bajaj absorbed part of the increase and launched 350cc versions.
150cc+ growing 20%+, 100-125cc low single digits in Q1FY27; the 100cc share of motorcycles fell from ~55% to ~46% over 5-7 years. Good for Bajaj's premium mix, bad for its volume share.
E-scooters reached ~25% of scooters by Q1FY27 (management); Chetak holds ~20-24% and is now EBITDA positive. Bajaj had no petrol scooter, so every EV sale is new business.
E-autos were 44% of the L5 segment in Q1FY27; Bajaj leads (33.5% of e-3W L5 in FY26) but its ICE share is 73.8%: the shift dilutes its dominance.
Bajaj's exports +21% in FY26 and +50% in Apr-Aug 2026; Latin America at records, Nigeria recovering. History shows sharp currency-driven busts (FY23-24).
Q1FY27 inflation ~4.5% of revenue; spreading to electronics, labour and logistics in Q2.
Realised USD/INR 94.4 in Q1FY27 vs 85.6 a year earlier; exports are 40-45% of revenue. Reverses if the rupee recovers.
Disrupted Chetak in H1FY26; alternate low-rare-earth motors restored supply by end-September 2025.
PM E-DRIVE for e-3W ran out at end-Q3FY26 (Bajaj absorbed it); PLI/PSI incentives were Rs1,040 cr in FY26 (~9% of standalone EBITDA).

ownership.src: BSE shareholding pattern via Screener.in (Jun-2026 categories); AR FY26 note 13 (holders above 5% and promoter list at 31-Mar-2026)
ownership.note: The number of shareholders more than doubled between March and June 2026 (to ~6.8 lakh), most likely small holders buying ahead of the July buyback tender. Named holders at Jun-2026 were not available to us.

moat: Export franchise in emerging markets
Strong
#1 in 9 of 15 key motorcycle export markets and 11 of 12 3W markets; ~50-60% retail share in Nigeria through ~800 own-brand stores; India's largest 2W exporter ($2.25 bn in FY26).
Hard to copy: decades of distribution, financing and service in Africa and LatAm.
Three-wheeler dominance
Strong but changing
73.8% of ICE 3Ws (87.9% of CNG); #1 in e-3W L5 at 33.5% within three years.
The EV shift lowers its share from three-quarters to one-third of the new segment; still the leader.
Premium/sports motorcycles and brands
Moderate-strong
Pulsar (Rs16,500 cr global revenue), Dominar, KTM and Triumph made in Chakan; KTM-Triumph 1.30 lakh domestic units in FY26; 125cc+ is 77.5% of its motorcycles.
Four brands in 125-400cc give pricing power above the commuter segment.
Domestic commuter motorcycles
Weak
Share of domestic motorcycles fell from 18.2% (FY24) to 15.6% (FY26); management concedes the 100-125cc segments.
No moat here; Hero, Honda and TVS are stronger.
Cost and margins
Strong
Standalone EBITDA margin 20.5% in FY26 and 20.9% in Q1FY27, the best among Indian 2W makers; spares ~Rs7,000 cr a year at record margins.
Scale in exports and 3Ws plus R&D-led design keep costs low.
Electric two-wheelers
Moderate
Chetak ~20-24% share, EBITDA positive, but demand exceeds its 50-60k a month capacity; TVS, Ather and others compete hard.
A real business now, but no structural edge over TVS.
Captive finance (BACL)
Moderate
AUM ~Rs20,000 cr, ROE >25%, 40-45% penetration of Bajaj sales.
Supports sales; a young book (credit cost ~3.9%) not yet tested in a downturn.
KTM
Uncertain
Iconic premium brands and 29 motorsport titles in 2025, but two years of losses, EUR827 m net debt and EBIT just positive in Q2 2026.
An option on a turnaround, not yet a moat that earns money.
critiques: Bajaj keeps losing domestic motorcycle share (18.2% FY24 to 15.6% FY26; Q1FY27 2W Vahan share -60 bp YoY) and is choosing to cede the 100-125cc mass market.
Margins lean on the weak rupee: realised USD/INR rose from 85.6 to 94.4 in a year; a rupee rebound would hit export realisations as commodity inflation broadens.
Exports have boom-bust history: Nigeria went from ~50,000 bikes a month to under 5,000 in 2023-24; Nigeria's current surge is partly pre-election institutional buying.
PLI/PSI incentives (Rs1,040 cr in FY26, doubled) are ~9% of standalone EBITDA and time-bound.
KTM adds EUR827 m of net debt and losses to the consolidated accounts; the turnaround is early (Q2 2026 EBIT EUR1.3 m).
BACL grows 70% a year with ~3.9% credit cost; a captive lender to rural and e-3W buyers is not tested through a cycle.
The street pays 23-25x FY28E standalone EPS, above Bajaj's own ~19x median forward P/E since 2021.
gaps: Chetak volumes by quarter in FY27 and Chetak revenue for FY26 (management said FY26 Chetak 'crossed the 5-lakh unit mark at Rs4,000 cr', but the AR shows 3.03 lakh domestic units; we use the AR).
Revenue and EBITDA by product (motorcycles, 3W, EV, spares) are not disclosed; our build uses domestic vs export revenue only.
PLI-Auto incentive: the exact end year of Bajaj's eligibility and the FY27 accrual were not found; we keep other operating revenue rising modestly.

Bajaj Mobility's full-year 2026 guidance is qualitative; KTM's contribution under Ind AS (Bajaj's books) differs from Bajaj Mobility's IFRS numbers (Q1FY27: +Rs322 cr EBITDA in Bajaj's line vs EUR5.5 m IFRS) and cannot be fully reconciled from public data.
BAIH BV's own net cash after KTM repaid its loans in Feb-2026 is not disclosed; the SOTP does not add it.
Named institutional holders at Jun-2026; Sep-2026 quarter volumes (released 1-Oct-2026, after our as-of date).
BACL quarterly finance cost for Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 is derived (operating profit less PBDT from Capital Market data), not from the filed results; Q2FY26 is the FY26 residual.
A post-results consensus EPS dated by 30-Sep-2026 was not found; we compare with five brokers' published estimates.
conflicts: Chetak FY26 volume: Q4FY26 call 'crossed the 5-lakh unit mark'; AR FY26 Table 2: 3,02,674 domestic units (we use the AR; the call figure may include exports or be cumulative to a different base).
FY26 exports: AR Table 4 $2,253 m; ICICI Direct shows $2,300 m; the Q4FY26 call says 'USD 2.2 billion' (we use the AR).
BACL: consolidated BACL borrowings Rs16,068 cr vs BACL's own Rs16,267 cr (the difference is likely Tier 2 debt held by Bajaj Auto, eliminated on consolidation).
